it's easy to find data that confirms whatever bias you want to hold about the market right now

bull or bear

for example:

you could use Q4 seasonality and the 4-year cycle theory to argue that R/R favors upside from here

or you could highlight historical crypto performance around US midterms to argue that we go lower

both sides can build a convincing case if they cherry-pick the right data

but when you zoom out and focus on what's happening RIGHT NOW:

- US equities losing trillions in market value amid the accelerating sell-off
- Asian markets suffering a major tech-driven rout
- AI-driven cybersecurity risks escalating, with potentially serious implications for global digital infrastructure
- the US-Iran war escalating, with the risk of further military action remaining a major wildcard... especially once Trump no longer has to worry about an imminent election
- the situation deteriorating across Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf region
- US macro data coming in less favorably than many had anticipated

and yet $BTC has refused to break down decisively despite all of the above

if bitcoin is absorbing this much uncertainty without a major breakdown, how easy is it to make a convincing case that the market is about to get significantly worse from here?

not saying it can't happen

but ignoring how well $BTC has held up while focusing exclusively on bearish historical patterns is just as much of a bias as blindly expecting Q4 seasonality to save us

When Starlink saved two lives in a California river.

Two people were trapped on the roof of their Jeep in the South Fork Carson River. Water was rising, and the vehicle had started moving in the current.

There was no mobile signal. But they had Starlink and a battery pack.

They used it to contact 775 Off Road and Recovery, share their location. A California Highway Patrol helicopter arrived and lifted both people to safety.

The rescue team said their Starlink call likely saved their lives.

This is why Starlink matters. A working connection can mean the difference between life and death.

This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.
